from io import BytesIO
from math import isclose
from pathlib import Path
from zipfile import ZipFile
import re
from openpyxl import load_workbook

file = Path(\"Matinee attendance calculations.xlsx\")
clean = BytesIO()
with ZipFile(file) as source, ZipFile(clean, \"w\") as dest:
    for member in source.infolist():
        payload = source.read(member.filename)
        if member.filename == \"docProps/app.xml\":
            payload = re.sub(rb\"<(Application|AppVersion)>["'^<]+</'"\\1>\", b\"\", payload)
        dest.writestr(member, payload)
file.write_bytes(clean.getvalue())

expected = {
    6: [4, 293, 239, 239/293, (58/72 + 67/80 + 55/66 + 59/75)/4],
    7: [4, 299, 223, 223/299, (49/69 + 68/82 + 54/77 + 52/71)/4],
    12: [3, 213, 172, 172/213, (58/72 + 55/66 + 59/75)/3],
    13: [3, 217, 155, 155/217, (49/69 + 54/77 + 52/71)/3],
}
for path in (file, Path(\"/private/tmp/matinee.0Vz3DG/recalc\")/file):

**Use the one-day reminder as the provisional default.** Across all eight matinees, weighted attendance was 81.6% with a one-day reminder and 74.6% with a three-day reminder. The one-day group also led when each show counted equally, and the gap widened after excluding the two school-holiday shows. Staffing availability determined reminder timing, so the comparison leaves the causal effect uncertain.
